notes: A subagent's body is its system prompt, and nothing in it is an import: "The frontmatter defines the subagent's metadata and configuration. The body becomes the system prompt that guides the subagent's behavior." The page states no import, and in Claude Code 2.1.303 only the loading of the memory files calls the include loader (F1), which no subagent loader calls.

"A custom output style is a Markdown file: frontmatter for metadata, then the instructions for Claude." The page states no import, and in Claude Code 2.1.303 no output style loader calls the include loader (F1).

A skill or a command attaches the files that its @ names when it is invoked, not when Claude Code loads its configuration: "In a regular session, skill descriptions are loaded into context so Claude knows what's available, but full skill content only loads when invoked." and "Custom commands have been merged into skills.", so the same holds for .claude/commands.

Claude Code Review includes a file only where a line of the root REVIEW.md holds @ and the name of a file beside REVIEW.md, or the path of a skill's SKILL.md, and nothing else, so an @path inside a line, as Claude Code reads it in a CLAUDE.md, and an @ with a path into a subdirectory other than .claude/skills/<folder>/SKILL.md are no includes: "To include a file, add a line to the root REVIEW.md with only @ and the file name on it." "Except for a skill file, a path into a subdirectory such as @docs/review-rules.md isn't included." "Source: copy guidance from any other file under .claude/, or from a bundled, personal, or plugin skill, into a file beside REVIEW.md. You can't include those directly." "A line whose name matches no file beside REVIEW.md stays in REVIEW.md as plain text". claude-import-07 reads the includes.

A Markdown link of the root REVIEW.md, or of a file that it includes, names a file that Claude Code Review does not include: "One level: list every file in the root REVIEW.md. An @ line in an included file or in a subdirectory REVIEW.md stays as plain text (skill files differ), and a Markdown link to another file isn't an include." The links count only toward the limit of links, past which the review skips the whole root REVIEW.md: "Links: keep Markdown links at 64 or fewer across REVIEW.md and the files it includes." claude-import-07 reads the includes.

VS Code reads a Markdown link of an instructions file as an import only with a setting that is off: "A link doesn't guarantee that the document's contents reach the model.", and "In Local, chat.includeReferencedInstructions ... controls automatic inclusion of referenced instructions and is off by default." (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/custom-instructions-reference). The AI settings reference (https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/ai-settings) gives chat.includeReferencedInstructions, "Automatically add instruction files referenced via Markdown links to Local chat requests.", the default false, and _addReferencedInstructions of computeAutomaticInstructions.ts returns unless the setting is on or the mode is Edit. The setting came with microsoft/vscode 0f484117 on 2026-01-22. The same function decides whether VS Code attaches a #file: reference of an instructions file (_addReferencedInstructions, promptFileParser.ts 494-515), which it therefore does not attach either. The same holds for .github/copilot-instructions.md.
"File references are not expanded in GEMINI.md or *.instructions.md files." The native resolver of Copilot CLI 1.0.98 returned a GEMINI.md with its @ lines as written.
"File references are not expanded in GEMINI.md or *.instructions.md files." The native resolver of Copilot CLI 1.0.98 returned a .instructions.md file with its @ lines as written.

Copilot CLI reads CLAUDE.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md and no CLAUDE.local.md: the page names "CLAUDE.md Agent instructions, discovered in the standard locations. Copilot CLI also uses .claude/CLAUDE.md." and no other Claude file, and the native resolver of Copilot CLI 1.0.98, started at the root, in .claude and in a subdirectory with a CLAUDE.local.md, also with child instructions turned on, listed no CLAUDE.local.md or .claude/CLAUDE.local.md. It listed no AGENTS.override.md either.

"Rule content reaches Agent as written. A file mention like @migration-template.sql tells Agent where to look, and Agent reads the file with its tools when it needs the content. The file's contents are not inlined into the prompt, and this is the same in the editor, the CLI, and Cloud Agents."

Cursor's staff, in its forum: Colin on 2026-10-07 (forum.cursor.com/t/file-references-in-cursor-rules-mdc-are-not-expanded-by-the-cli-agent/173952/5): "an @notes.md line inside a rule (or AGENTS.md) is passed to the agent as a pointer, not inlined, and that's the same in the editor and the CLI."

Cursor CLI reads CLAUDE.md as a rule, and the content of a rule reaches the agent as written: "The CLI also reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the project root (if present) and applies them as rules alongside .cursor/rules." The rules page (https://cursor.com/docs/rules): "Rule content reaches Agent as written. A file mention like @migration-template.sql tells Agent where to look, and Agent reads the file with its tools when it needs the content. The file's contents are not inlined into the prompt, and this is the same in the editor, the CLI, and Cloud Agents." For AGENTS.md, cursor-not-import-02 records the same.

Codex has no import syntax and reads each file as it is: "Merge order: Codex concatenates files from the root down, joining them with blank lines." read_agents_md of codex-rs/core/src/agents_md.rs pushes the text of each file and reads no @. The format itself has none: "No. AGENTS.md is just standard Markdown." (https://github.com/agentsmd/agents.md/blob/342016eb22df3fb94a85bec29272e666defa83eb/components/FAQSection.tsx).

A custom command injects the file that @{path} names when it runs, not when Gemini CLI loads its memory: "File injection: @{path/to/file.txt} is replaced by the content of file.txt." and "The command searches for the path in the current directory and any other workspace directories."

Antigravity's bare @filename does not inline the file: "@filename: Does not inline file contents. Instead, it resolves the path (relative to the rule file, or as a workspace-relative/absolute path) and rewrites it to a canonical absolute workspace path (@/workspace/path) so the agent has an unambiguous file reference." Antigravity CLI 1.4.2 inlined no bare @../inc/a.md. The changelog of the app's 2.11.0 (https://antigravity.google/docs/changelog), "Added support for referencing and inlining external files directly using @path/to/file syntax within AGENTS.md and custom rule files.", writes the form that the page and the CLI do not inline. The same holds for AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md.

The includes of a model_decision or a manual rule reach the model only when the agent requests the rule or the user mentions it in the Antigravity App, which is no context that the configuration loads, as for a skill of Claude Code (claude-not-import-03): "model_decision (best for detailed domain guides): Antigravity injects only the rule's path and description upfront (progressive disclosure). The agent reads the full rule on demand when your task matches the description." and "manual (explicit @ mention only): Antigravity never loads these rules automatically. Antigravity adds the rule to your message only when you @-mention it (ideal for release checklists or audit rubrics). The Antigravity CLI doesn't support rule mentions". The same holds for the rules of the other rule rows of import_patterns.csv.

A custom command of OpenCode 2 imports nothing: "Stored templates do not expand @path; it remains ordinary prompt text." In OpenCode 1 (https://docs.opencode.ai/docs/commands/), a custom command includes the file that its @ names when the command runs, not when OpenCode loads its configuration: "Custom commands let you specify a prompt you want to run when that command is executed in the TUI." and "Include files in your command using @ followed by the filename." The same holds for .opencode/command and for the template of a command in the command key of the configuration.
